pairs.reviewNote: Compared the opening, argument and ending: the Eshkol valley, foreknowledge, Abraham’s friend and the future cluster agree. The English edition also prints the full biblical verse at the start; this differs from the abbreviated quotation in the Hebrew.
Compared the Ovot, Iyei HaAvarim, Zered and Arnon sequence. English prints the initial biblical verse in full and includes explanatory notes.
Compared the troop counts, pairing, reluctance and drawing lots. English prints opening verses in full and includes explanatory notes.

Compared Nadav and Avihu, the offered fire, and the final cross-reference. Both editions abbreviate the cross-reference to Vayikra Rabbah. The English edition adds the full opening biblical verse and explanatory notes.

pairs.boundaryNote: English source section 9 contains both Hebrew 20:9 and the beginning of 20:10. Split at its internal section-10 marker, removed that marker, and joined the remainder with English source section 10. Biblical quotations and translator notes are retained.

English source section 9 contains both Hebrew 20:9 and the beginning of 20:10. Split at its internal section-10 marker, removed that marker, and joined the remainder with English source section 10. Biblical quotations and translator notes are retained.

The source English includes a Rabba bar bar Ḥana episode absent from the retained Hebrew edition between the fortified place in Gehenna and the future redemption. That episode is omitted here and marked with an ellipsis; the original source remains separately available.
The Hebrew source is explicitly marked partial and lists six names only. The English source continues with explanations of those names; only its first sentence is linked.
The Hebrew excerpt ends immediately after introducing a citation from Isaiah. The English source continues with the quotation; it is omitted here to reflect the retained Hebrew boundary.

The Hebrew source is marked partial and ends with the nations of the world. The source translation continues with a banquet story, which is not in the available Hebrew passage and is excluded from this paired excerpt.

The Hebrew contains several isolated opening fragments, followed by a coherent comparison of passages on theft from an Israelite and a convert. Only the English corresponding to that latter comparison is linked; the incomplete opening fragments are visibly identified as untranslated.

The retained Hebrew skips a series of stories between the scorpion and the proverb, and further stories between the proverb and the hornet passage. Those source-only English sections are omitted with visible ellipses; the full source is separately available.
Only the continuous Rabbi Levi passage ending with Proverbs 31:1 is included; the source has additional material before and after it.
The English source includes two explanatory stories absent from the retained Hebrew; both are omitted with visible markers. The opening and closing arguments were compared.

The Hebrew begins within the eternal-Temple interpretation and explicitly ends unfinished after the swine-and-creeping-things analogy. The corresponding English span is extracted; source material before and after is outside this Hebrew excerpt.

method: Manually compared Hebrew and English openings and endings and checked matching chapter and section; English source exactly matches existing local text.
limitations: 232 selected passage pairs were reviewed, including explicitly marked partial excerpts; unmatched passages remain blank. Source license and release obligations still need review.
